chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: Jazz musicians in Europe and Japan
summary: Royal comments on English, Swedish and German musicians, American studio hires in Germany, and Japanese players as great copyists.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Did you ever get a chance to hear any music anyplace (inaudible)?

Yes, you hear music quite a bit. You hear very good music quite often. The English have some very good musicians. The Swedish were the first to come out with some good musicians. Only there were just a few of them, then the Germand came on with a big rush and came out with some very fine musicians. Of course, they imported a whole lot of Americans into those studio bands and things in Germany. Every big studio orchestra in every big city has Americans mixed into
it to get the flavor and find out what's done about it and they're doing something about it. They're making very big strides.

Then, all of a sudden, after the end of World War II, the Japanese suddenly became Americanized and they have come on with some wonderful musicians. They have some guys that can just play like mad because they study very hard and the mechanics of the instruments, they learn very well and they go over and over and over and over and over, until they get it out. As you found out in optical equipment -- cameras, whatever you have, even down to the -- to rivaling and surpassing the American automobile --
We had an interruption there. You were talking about Japan.

Yeah, I last mentioned about rivaling the American automobile and certain lines of the -- especially the small ones. They are perfectionists in their lines and along with their musical playings, they've become quite adept at being professionals also. They're great copyists. They haven't come in with anything which could be put down as being original in jazz lines, but they can take the fellows that they like very well, like Cannonball Adderley and people of that sort, and they can mimic them very, very well and sound good.
